messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — Q3 forecast shows ~27% GPU-hour bump in APAC during promo week (7/12-7/18). Roughly +12.4k GPU-hours. This will pressure the small-slice/interactive pool first. Running sims now, will post numbers. :warning:
infra-monitor-bot: Automated forecast: apac cluster usage +31% over baseline for next 7d. See dashboard: https://dash.redwood/apac/forecast
Sanjay Patel: Can we push more throughput to Dedicated or throttle low-priority embeddings? What's current soft-preempt budget?
Kai Ortega: soft-preempt budget = 6% total hours. avg preempt latency ~120s. slab_free_ratio (frag) = 0.32 right now — lots of 0.25/0.5 slice requests creating holes.
Dina Li: We disabled aggressive compaction during the network maintenance last month — can we re-enable or tune frequency for the promo window?
Maya Chen: Quick sim results: moving ~18% of small/embedding jobs to a shared-small-pool reduces slab_frag to ~0.18 and saves ~9% infra cost, but raises chat tail (p90->p90+45ms). Tradeoff: cost vs tail-latency.
Kai Ortega: Paste of the sim command + key lines:
```bash
python tools/binpack_sim.py --cohorts=5 --quantiles=8 --spike=1.27 --seed=42
# output:
# baseline_frag=0.32, baseline_cost=100%
# shared_pool_frag=0.18, cost=91%, chat_p90+45ms
```
Sanjay Patel: That latency hit is unacceptable for interactive chat customers. Embeddings/batch can be moved. Can we route chat to hotter nodes (reserved) and embeddings to the shared pool?
Maya Chen: Proposed short-term plan:
- create ephemeral "burst-cohort" (8 nodes) for promo (7d)
- pin chat models to 30% of small-slice capacity (reserved)
- make remaining small-slice capacity preemptible and eligible for shared embeddings pool
- increase compaction frequency to every 5m during promo window
This should avoid most chat tail impact while reclaiming capacity for embeddings.
Henry (ops-bot): Reserving 30% small-slice = ~240 GPU-hours/day for chat. Estimated incremental infra spend ~ $3.2k/day (on top of usual).
Dina Li: Also: can we auto-fallback low-priority customers to quantized variants (int8) for embeddings? Redwood Optimize has a candidate list.
Kai Ortega: Scheduler-level change suggestion: adopt quantile-fit packing for small slices — group requests by sequence-length quantiles and pack accordingly; reduces KV cache fragmentation. I pushed a PR for the scheduler heuristics (link in PR).
Sanjay Patel: Approve a canary rollout: apac-north1 only, 2h canary window, watch metrics: preempt_rate, chat_99_latency, slab_frag. If chat_99 > +150ms or slab_frag > 0.25 -> rollback.
Maya Chen: I'll schedule the canary at 0100 UTC tonight. @Dina please wire alerts to oncall; @Kai please ensure automated rollback & mitigate script ready. :white_check_mark:
infra-monitor-bot: Canary scheduled by Maya for ts=1729464000. Monitor channels: #incidents, #eng-sre. Good luck :rocket:
Kai Ortega: Simulation summary (short): expected net saved GPU-hours over 7 days = ~6.8k. Worst-case customer-impact scenario increases tail for <0.6% of queries. Logs attached to PR (summary only).
Dina Li: I'll draft alert runbook and an oncall playbook for rollback steps and customer comms.
Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll iterate after the canary. If we see frag improving without tail regressions, plan is to scale the shared pool and keep compaction at 5m for the promo window.
Sanjay Patel: Also recommend we enable cost telemetry for the reserved vs preempt pool per-customer so finance can reconcile the extra spend daily.
Maya Chen: Good call. Will add to the canary dashboard.
Kai Ortega: thumbs up. I'll monitor and be oncall during the canary window.
Henry (ops-bot): Canary started (simulated) at 1729464000. Metric watchlist active.
